This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #36737: Same root cause — postinstall blocked by `allowScripts` leaves a broken binary stub — reported on `opencode-ai` v1 (Windows), but the underlying packaging issue is the same as described here for `@opencode/cli` v2.

Confirming this on V2 (opencode 2.0.3, Windows), same model, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free` via Console. In our case the poisoned turn broke mid-tool-chain, and everything after it failed for a day: service-restart drains, fresh prompts, and compaction all hit the same 400. That's both of @unurgunite's triggers in one session.

A heads-up for anyone on 2.x trying the plugin: v0.2.0 loads cleanly on V2 but is a no-op there. It walks the V1 shapes (`part.metadata.openai.*` with `part.time.start`), while V2 puts the crypto in two other places:

- persisted parts: `part.state.{itemId, reasoningEncryptedContent}`, timestamp at `part.time.created` (some of ours carry `reasoningEncryptedContent: null` with a bare itemId)
- the context-hook payload is the AI SDK shape: crypto under `part.providerMetadata.openai,` and `part.time` is empty, so blob age is unknowable on that path

I dumped the hook payload to verify: reasoning parts arrive as `{type, text, providerMetadata}` with no `state` and `time: {}`. The V1 relevance check (non-empty string blob) never matches, so nothing gets stripped and the poison replays untouched. This matters for @pascalthedev's 2.0.3 report above, where new sessions die at the first tool call.

One more V2 quirk: plugin `console.error` does not reach `opencode.log` on V2. We had zero `[sanitize-reasoning]` log lines while the hook was verifiably firing, so the README's "look for `stripped N stale reasoning blob(s)`" check cannot confirm anything on V2. A file dump is the only way we could see what the hook receives.

I run a local fork with V2 support added (same TTL and kill-switch semantics, upstream's 14 tests pass unmodified): V2 holders strip on any itemId/blob key, since a bare itemId is rejected as "item not found" under store=false; no-timestamp parts fail safe to strip; and the hook registers for all model-request kinds (context/compaction/generate/title), because compaction replays the same reasoning and fails the same way. With it, the one-day-dead session replies again and a tool-call round trip through Muse Spark completes. Happy to open a PR against the plugin repo with these changes if useful.

@pompompur-in's IP-binding report matches what we can see from here: whether a request fails depends only on whether the gateway's current upstream caller is the one that issued the stored blobs. A restart is just one way to end up on a different caller.

New data point, possibly useful even though this is closed "not planned": the global skill catalog appears to be a real contributing factor.

On Windows, OpenCode 1.18.27, `ollama` provider via `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`. I had ~192 skills discoverable across `~/.claude/skills/` + `~/.agents/skills/` (mostly unrelated Claude Code marketplace skills). `opencode debug skill` confirmed `init count=191` at session start, with skill descriptions alone totaling ~10.7k tokens — about a third of a 32k-context local model's budget before the conversation even starts.

With that catalog in place, I reliably reproduced the compaction loop described in this issue with 3 of 4 local models on a moderately complex coding task (repeated "Objective/Important Details/Work State..." blocks, never converging). After temporarily moving both skill directories out of OpenCode's scan path (`init count=1`), the same task on the same models completed the loop pattern 0/3 times in repeat runs — the loop symptom didn't reappear, though generic slowness and separate tool-calling issues (see #7083) remained.

Not claiming this is the whole root cause — but for anyone hitting this with a large personal/global skill catalog installed, pruning it (or checking `opencode debug skill` for the count) seems worth trying before giving up on local providers entirely.

Confirming this with 3 different local models via `ollama` provider (`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`, OpenCode 1.18.27, Windows), same coding task each time ("create a single-file Snake game"):

- `qwen2.5-coder:14b`: emitted the exact tool-call JSON as a markdown text block in the chat response (`{"name": "write", "arguments": {...}}`), never actually invoked. Second attempt (with a renamed model tag, see below) produced malformed JSON with mixed array/object syntax and a pseudo-syntax `[tool_call: write for content '...' to file_path '...']` — still not executed.
- `gpt-oss:20b`: didn't even attempt tool-call syntax — just returned the complete, correct code as a fenced markdown block, as if it were a plain chat completion.
- `devstral:24b`: outright refused ("I'm unable to create the file you're asking for") — traced this to the model's own baked-in system prompt (`ollama show devstral:24b --modelfile` shows `"You are Devstral... using the OpenHands scaffold"`), which appears to override whatever tool-use instructions OpenCode provides.

One partial, reproducible mitigation for some models (not all): OpenCode selects its provider-specific system prompt file by matching the model ID string (`packages/opencode/src/session/system.ts`, per a public gist walkthrough of the prompt pipeline) — anything not matching a known provider falls back to a generic `qwen.txt`. Renaming a model with `ollama cp <model> gemini-<anything>` (so it matches the `gemini` branch instead) fixed this cleanly for `gemma4:12b-it-qat` (3/3 clean runs, real tool execution, no narration) but had zero effect on `devstral:24b` (blocked by its own baked-in system prompt) or `qwen2.5-coder:14b` (same JSON-as-text narration, alias or not). So: real, cheap to try, but not a general fix — model-dependent.

+1 from our side, with a matching crash.

We run 1.18.30 (embedded Bun 1.3.14) on WSL2: `opencode serve` under a systemd user unit with `Restart=on-failure`. Three crashes in two days, each one:

```
panic(main thread): Bus error at address 0x767D80048ABE
oh no: Bun has crashed. This indicates a bug in Bun, not your code.
```

Systemd recorded `status=4/ILL`, and the kernel reported the trap at `ip:2607064`. That's the address the core dumps in #40219 were traced to, which points at the ByteStream use-after-free fixed in oven-sh/bun#31963. If the shared address holds up, the runtime bump is what fixes it.

Two things that might help triage. We only see this under `serve`, and memory looks ordinary at crash time (RSS 0.86GB, peak 3.22GB). There's also about 44s between the panic printing and systemd reaping the process, so the real outage runs longer than `RestartSec` suggests.

Caveat: our Sep 13 trap lines had rotated out of the journal, so the address match rests on one crash, and we haven't disassembled the binary to confirm the site.

#40812 shows the same pattern on `serve` with 1.3.14, so it isn't just us.
At the very least, the session list on the left must be kept! Is Opencode actually not open at all? Who made this decision on behalf of everyone?

Hi, a quick follow-up on this. It adds exponential backoff for streams that never connect, so the Basic auth prompt stops re-triggering every second (issue #47062). Streams that connected once before dropping still reconnect at the normal interval. CI is green. Would appreciate a review when someone has a minute -- glad to rebase on the latest v2 if needed.
